This optional track keeps the practical systems visible while adding the mathematics and modelling used in post-secondary engineering. Use the linked package when it exists; later topics remain planned rather than pretending to be complete.

## Circuit analysis

Analyze voltage, current, resistance, power, and energy in computers, vehicles, batteries, sensors, motors, and robots. Start with [Series Circuits](../circuits/series-circuits.qmd) to apply Ohm's law, then use the [circuits package sequence](../circuits/index.qmd) for parallel, mixed, Kirchhoff, and matrix methods.

Textbook reference: *Grob's Basic Electronics*, supported by the Problems Manual and Experiments Manual. Public pages cite chapters and problem families without publishing scans.

## Measurement and data

Record repeatable measurements with units, uncertainty, and enough metadata to interpret the test later. Use [Python Measurement Logging](../linux-operating-systems/python-data-logging.qmd) and [Python Analysis and Curve Fitting](../linux-operating-systems/python-analysis-curve-fitting.qmd).

## Computing and control

Connect operating systems, networking, programming, sensors, outputs, and feedback in recognizable systems. Continue through the [Linux and Operating Systems path](../linux-operating-systems/index.qmd) while the dedicated robotics and control packages are developed.

## Ontario course collaboration opportunities {#ontario-course-collaboration-opportunities}

TEJ3M and TEJ4M provide the computer-engineering context. SPH3U can support energy, measurement, and motion; SCH4U can support batteries and material systems; SBI4U can support sensor investigations where the electronics are the instrument, not a substitute for the biology. These connections identify useful collaboration, not course equivalencies.
